desc:
Each event is [startDay, endDay, value]. It takes place on every day from startDay to endDay inclusive, and attending it earns value. You can only be at one event per day, so two attended events must not share any day: if you attend an event ending on day d, the next event must start on day d + 1 or later.

You may attend at most k events. Return the largest total value you can collect.

events = [[1, 3, 5], [2, 4, 6], [4, 6, 3], [5, 7, 4]], k = 2  ->  10

The best choice is [2, 4, 6] and [5, 7, 4].
constraints: events[i] = [startDay, endDay, value] with 1 ≤ startDay ≤ endDay ≤ 10<sup>9</sup> and 1 ≤ value ≤ 10<sup>5</sup>
Events are in no particular order
hints: Without the limit k this would be weighted interval scheduling. The limit adds a second dimension to the state.

Sort events by start day. Let dp[j][i] be the best value using at most j events chosen among events i, i+1, .... For event i you either skip it or take it and jump to the first event that starts after it ends.
Find that next event with binary search on the sorted start days. Then dp[j][i] = max(dp[j][i+1], value[i] + dp[j-1][next[i]]). Only the previous layer j-1 is needed.
editorial: Sort the events by start day and precompute next[i], the index of the first event whose start day is greater than end[i] (binary search with bisect_right on the start days). Define dp[j][i] as the maximum value obtainable from events with index at least i using at most j of them, with dp[j][n] = 0 and dp[0][i] = 0.

Transition: skip event i (dp[j][i+1]) or attend it and continue after it (value[i] + dp[j-1][next[i]]). Take the maximum. Because the transition for layer j reads only layer j-1, two arrays of length n + 1 suffice. The answer is dp[k][0].

A greedy choice by value or by earliest end fails because of the cap k and the differing values. Time is O(n log n + k·n), space O(n). The largest answer is 3,000 × 10<sup>5</sup>, which fits in 32 bits.
solution:
from bisect import bisect_right


def maxValueKEvents(events, k):
    ev = sorted(events)
    n = len(ev)
    starts = [e[0] for e in ev]
    nxt = [bisect_right(starts, e[1]) for e in ev]
    prev = [0] * (n + 1)
    for _ in range(k):
        cur = [0] * (n + 1)
        for i in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
            take = ev[i][2] + prev[nxt[i]]
            cur[i] = take if take > cur[i + 1] else cur[i + 1]
        prev = cur
    return prev[0]
